questions.question: Compare IRQ and FIQ exceptions with respect to latency and register usage.
questions.solution_html:
• Latency:
  • • FIQ (Fast Interrupt Request): Lower latency → faster response (handled with
  • higher priority and minimal overhead)
  • • IRQ (Interrupt Request): Higher latency compared to FIQ
  • Register Usage:
  • • FIQ: Has more banked registers (R8–R14), so it can operate without
  • saving/restoring many registers → faster execution
  • • IRQ: Fewer banked registers (only R13–R14), so it often needs to save/restore
  • registers → slower than FIQ

questions.question: List and discuss the design principles of Embedded System.
questions.solution_html:
• Any five give (5 mark)
  • Real-Time Operation
  • Embedded systems must respond within strict time constraints.
  • • Hard real-time: Missing a deadline = system failure
  • • Soft real-time: Occasional delays are acceptable
  • Reliability
  • Systems should operate continuously without failure.
  • • Important in critical applications like automotive, medical devices
  • • Requires fault tolerance and robust design
  • Efficiency (Performance & Power)
  • • Must use minimal resources (CPU, memory)
  • • Low power consumption is crucial, especially for battery-powered devices
  • Cost Effectiveness
  • • Hardware and software should be optimized to reduce overall cost
  • • Selection of components is based on budget and requirements
  • Compact Size
  • • Embedded systems are often part of small devices
  • • Requires minimal hardware footprint and optimized PCB design
  • Application-Specific Design
  • • Designed for a specific task (not general-purpose)
  • • Improves performance and efficiency
  • Scalability and Flexibility
  • • Design should allow future upgrades or modifications
  • • Modular approach helps reuse components
  • Hardware-Software Co-Design
  • • Hardware and software are developed together for optimal performance
  • • Trade-offs are made between hardware complexity and software flexibility
  • Low Power Consumption
  • • Essential for portable and IoT devices
  • • Techniques include sleep modes, power gating
  • Robustness
  • • Must handle environmental conditions (temperature, noise, vibration)
  • • Includes error detection and recovery mechanisms

questions.question: Explain the Cortex-M memory map
questions.solution_html:
• The ARM Cortex-M memory map defines how the entire address space (4 GB) is
  • organized into different regions for code, data, and peripherals.
  • Total Address Space
  • • Cortex-M uses a 32-bit address space → 4 GB (0x00000000 to 0xFFFFFFFF)
  • Address Range Region Description
  • 0x00000000 – 0x1FFFFFFF Code Region Program memory (Flash), interrupt vectors
  • 0x20000000 – 0x3FFFFFFF SRAM Region Data memory (RAM)
  • 0x40000000 – 0x5FFFFFFF Peripheral Region Memory-mapped I/O registers
  • 0x60000000 – 0x9FFFFFFF External RAM External memory (if available)
  • 0xA0000000 – 0xDFFFFFFF External Devices External peripherals
  • 0xE0000000 – 0xFFFFFFFF System Region NVIC, system control, debug components

questions.question: Compare ODR and IDR registers in ARM Cortex-M GPIO.
questions.solution_html:
• ODR (Output Data Register)
  • • Used to write data to GPIO pins
  • • Controls the output state (HIGH or LOW)
  • • Applicable when pin is configured as OUTPUT
  • • Writing: o 1 → sets pin HIGH o 0 → sets pin LOW IDR (Input Data Register)
  • • Used to read data from GPIO pins
  • • Reflects the current logic level at the pin
  • • Applicable when pin is configured as INPUT
  • • Reading: o 1 → pin is HIGH o 0 → pin is LOW Feature ODR IDR Full form Output Data Register Input Data Register Operation Write Read Purpose Control output pins Read input pins Direction CPU → Pin Pin → CPU Usage mode Output mode Input mode

questions.question: What is the use of the `volatile` keyword in Embedded C? [5x6 = 30]
questions.solution_html:
• The volatile keyword in Embedded C is used to tell the compiler that a
  • variable’s value can change unexpectedly, outside the normal program flow. This
  • prevents the compiler from applying certain optimizations that assume the value
  • doesn’t change on its own.
  • Purpose
  • • Ensures the compiler always reads the variable from memory, rather than using a
  • cached value in a register.
  • • Commonly used for:
  • o Hardware registers (GPIO, timers, ADCs)
  • o Global variables modified in interrupts
  • o Shared memory in multi-threaded or RTOS applications
